evidence: Source/parser review only (tomllib parse of scoring.toml and all five judge.toml files, byte comparison with the frozen template); this is not a run of the private check-rubric-schema.py / check-scoring-policy.py and not a configured judge run on these bytes. (1) tests/scoring.toml is byte-identical to the template: [gates] render = 0.0, constraints = 0.0; [weights] functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2 (sum 1.0); [floors] functional = 0.05; the directories tests/gates/{render,constraints} and tests/scored/{functional,polish,visual} all exist, each with judge.toml and prompt.md, so the fixed dimensions sit in the right suite. (2) Every judge.toml has [judge] judge = "claude-code" (matches REWARDKIT_JUDGE in task.toml), mode = "batched", timeout, isolated = false, prompt_template = "prompt.md"; none has model, reasoning_effort, temperature or [judge].weight. The [judge] block and MCP declarations are identical to the template in all five files. (3) Every dimension declares the playwright stdio server (command playwright-mcp, args --headless --isolated --executable-path=/usr/local/bin/chromium --no-sandbox). Only scored/functional/judge.toml lines 14-18 declare the second server: name = "verifier", command = "/usr/local/bin/python3", args = ["/tests/tools/restart_mcp.py", "$APP_RESTART_HELPER"]. tests/test.sh line 193 has export APP_RESTART_HELPER="$LOG_DIR/app-restart.sh" after generating and chmod 755 the helper (lines 127-192); test.sh, tools/restart_mcp.py, tools/score.py and tests/Dockerfile are byte-identical to the template, and the Dockerfile copies /usr/local from the node runtime and COPY . /tests, so the path resolves. Exactly one criterion (cw_save_reload_restart) calls restart_app, consistent with the single-use tool, and functional/prompt.md line 31 names the restart_app tool of the verifier MCP server; no prompt sends the judge to a shell (each says never run shell or install commands). (4) Criteria: render 1 binary (all_pass), constraints 2 binary (all_pass), functional 42 binary (weighted_mean, weights 1.0/1.5/2.0), polish 6 binary, visual 3 likert with points = 5 exactly as the template. All 54 ids are unique across the task, id equals name, every weight is positive, every description is non-empty, every criterion has only the template's keys. Gates are binary only. (5) Prompts resolve: each prompt_template file exists, is LF, and contains exactly two placeholders, {app_context} and {criteria}; test.sh lines 195-201 substitute {app_context} from the non-empty tests/app_context.md (4050 bytes), which contains no braces, and no judge.toml description contains a brace, so no stray placeholder can break templating. (6) Budgets nest: gate judges 600 + 600 = 1200 < 1500; scored judges 9000 + 900 + 900 = 10800 < 11100; 1500 + 11100 = 12600 < [verifier].timeout_sec 13200. Counterexample attempts: a second dimension declaring the restart server, a duplicated id across dimensions, a likert gate criterion, a missing {criteria}, or a weight key in [judge] would each be a defect; none is present. Residual, not a defect of this row: the two workbook copies in the frozen rules differ in bytes (rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx sha256 6d44970b... versus harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/assets/WebDev_Rubrics_QC.xlsx d7b5d607...); I used the former as the assignment directs. The Internal Quality Checks sheet still words row 24 for the retired reward.toml layout; the Quality Checks sheet and the skill's staged contract are the current wording and were applied. No configured judge run exists for these exact bytes; the hosted run on an earlier candidate shows only that the same template wiring launched and graded there.
